heard: A $125 million NASA orbiter vanished behind Mars without a trace. In September 1999, the spacecraft fired its engine to enter orbit after a nine-month voyage. It slipped behind the red planet as planned, but its radio signal never returned. Tracking data revealed the probe had plunged to an altitude of just 57 kilometers. Its minimum survival altitude was 80 kilometers, leaving the probe incinerated in the atmosphere. Investigators traced the catastrophe to thruster software shared between two distant teams. Lockheed Martin in Colorado calculated thruster impulse using imperial pound-force seconds. NASA navigators in California expected metric newtons, a difference of 4.45 times.
